event_sentences: GameLook报道/对大部分的中小团队而言，最难解决的问题之一就是如何获得融资，但有时候，你看到一些投资新闻又会觉得别人拿钱真容易。
比如刚成立4个月的土耳其手游公司Loom Games，全公司都凑不出12个人，手里只有一款谁都说不准半年后还能不能打的游戏，但却快速被Scopely斥资10亿美元收购。
促成这笔交易的人，叫做Affan Butt，他牵头完成的游戏融资可不止这一笔。
另一个比较经典的案例是（软银投资）Supercell，2012年，他就发了一句“我想去你们公司坐坐”，Supercell 的 CEO Ilkka Paananen 回了个”Sure”。
Affan Butt 联合创办了 Aream & Co.，这家投行至今已为超过110笔游戏行业交易提供顾问服务，交易总价值高达400亿美元。
惊人的数据，正在融资。
Affan 问他们为什么融资而不是出售。
Affan 的公司将其以超过十亿美元的价格出售给了沙特背景的 Scopely。
七年间完成超过110笔交易，价值400亿美元，过去五年中游戏行业1亿美元以上的卖方交易有一半以上出自他们之手。
“2012年，我在 LinkedIn 上联系了 Ilkka Paananen（Supercell CEO兼联合创始人）。
Affan 飞到赫尔辛基，和 Ilkka 以及 Petteri 几乎待了一整天，Petteri 当时是 Supercell 的董事会主席，如今是传奇风投人。
《卡通农场》刚上线，《部落冲突》还在开发中，Sensor Tower 还不存在，所以没有什么数据可以用来提前预知未来。
正式的并购流程从首次接触到完成大约需要六个月。
如今收购方的池子也比过去更小了，这就是为什么竞购战可能适得其反。
收购方池子如今也比过去更小了，而且不是因为商业原因。
这会进入收购方的数据库。
他引用的案例是 Supercell 2013年的老股转让交易，从创始人到支持部门，每个人出售了16%的股票和已归属期权。
”土耳其创始人通常把老股转让解读为忠诚度测试，担心出售被视为缺乏承诺，而以色列创始人则每次融资都期待这一环节。
此外，游戏行业的 IPO 路径实际上已经关闭，因为2020-22年上市的那批公司表现惨淡。
买家想发布你的新游戏。
你不想，因为发布成本会吃掉你的对赌收益所依赖的数字。
芬兰的 ReWorks，被 Playtika 以6亿美元收购，是我一直反思的案例。

买家版图已经大变，因为很多买家自己也已被收购。
剩下的是公开市场的战略买家（如 Savvy）、拥有真实资产负债表的大型私人战略买家（如腾讯），如 Moon Active 和 Tripledot Studios、私募股权（如 CVC），以及包括韩国买家和印度 Nazara 在内的较新中市值入局者。
超过一定规模后，名单几乎完全缩减。
当我问这些不同类型的收购方暗中最在意什么时，他否定了这个前提。
没有 LP，没有基金存续期，不需要按别人的时间表退出，在能让普通买家冻结的危机中仍继续收购。
定义了过去十年的收购方有一半自己也被收购了，游戏行业的 IPO 之门关闭了，超过一定估值后，能开出支票的人一只手就数得过来，而且大多拿着大多数创始人没想到过的护照。
不是围绕不可持续增长或 AI 叙事的东西，而是一个他们想看到在余生里持续运转的工作室。

title: 苹果护城河塌了！App Store收入十年首次下滑，中国游戏成“全球手游顶梁柱”
event_sentences: 但同时，游戏圈先见证了另一个旧时代的落幕： 今年二季度App Store美国区支出十年来首次下滑。
其中不得不提到的是Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney，他几乎是以一己之力硬刚巨头苹果，投入巨资打官司，推动打破苹果谷歌对自家游戏生态、乃至整个APP市场的“生杀予夺”大权，促使各国监管下场调查苹果这位移动生态守门员，直接导致苹果自家地盘缩水、开发者分到了更多收益。
苹果电动车战略彻底失败就不说，新设备AR眼镜昂贵和成效不高，踌躇不前的苹果守着巨额现金搞股票回购、却迟迟在AI赛道毫无斩获，苹果Siri起了个大早、却没赶上AI大语言模型时代这班车。
如今AI时代的内存存储芯片价格暴涨、严重冲击了各种硬件，手机首当其冲，苹果进一步受到影响。
三家机构揭开同一真相：AppStore美区收入十年首次下滑
·根据Sensor Tower数据，2026年Q2美国消费者在苹果应用商店的支出，出现十年以来的首次下降；
根据Newzoo数据，全球玩家数量已经超过35亿。
甚至华为被美国政府制裁打压前，2018年Q2手机出货量曾经一度已经超过了苹果。
随着苹果在自己最重要的美国市场，出现十年来的首次收入下滑，更像是释放出了一个“拐点信号”：当苹果自家来自应用的收入不再增长，这艘APP和手游时代的巨轮该如何转向？
但随着吃鸡玩法爆发，手握全球现象级产品《堡垒之夜》的Epic一跃成为巨无霸级公司，游戏同时最高在线人数超千万，年营收达百亿美元级别。
未来游戏圈的投资可能变成“自己人玩”，只剩产业内资本和极少数游戏大佬还能顺利拿到融资。
这也眼红了苹果谷歌等渠道，比如谷歌去年就发布了自己的小游戏商店Instant Games。
换句话说，海外公司已经跟不上中国公司产品创新的节奏，双方对AI的态度也是一个重大分歧点。
当欧美公司和独立游戏团队还在对AI避之不及时，中国公司已经开始集体拥抱AI技术，不只是增效提质，而是针对不同类型、不同平台游戏体验创新，探索出了合适自己的AI方法论。
腾讯喊着“AI in Game”口号，在《和平精英》《暗区突围》等大DAU竞技游戏里实装AI 队友；网易《燕云十六声》《永劫无间》等旗舰级产品，也在大量使用AI丰富玩家体验、降低UGC创作门槛；米哈游走得更快，已在Steam发布《Whispers from the Star》 《BSide：Olivia Lin》等多款AI产品。
如今每一年发布会都要靠中国手游站台的苹果，是否会想起，十年前扭扭捏捏、不愿给中国游戏推荐位的自己？

title: “半个游戏圈都投了”！Tripo AI母公司VAST融资30亿元，三七,完美,延趣入局当股东
event_sentences: GameLook报道/游戏公司对AI 3D的投资仍在加速。
距离7月初宣布超10亿元融资仅过去约两个月，Tripo AI母公司VAST（三启万物）再次披露大额融资，完美世界、三七互娱、延趣游戏等游戏厂商出现在新一轮投资方名单中。
近日，VAST宣布完成B轮和B+轮融资，合计约30亿元人民币，由经纬创投领投。
据VAST披露，不到半年，VAST累计融资约50亿元人民币，刷新3D原生智能领域融资额纪录。
回看上一轮融资，游戏公司的参与已经相当突出。
今年7月2日，VAST宣布完成超10亿元A3战略轮融资，四三九九、贪玩游戏、巨人网络等游戏厂商，与吉利资本及多家投资机构共同参投。
如今，随着更多游戏厂商入局，这家成立于2023年的AI公司，正在吸引越来越多内容生产端的游戏产业资本。
这种关注背后，有一个游戏研发团队容易理解的需求，角色、道具、建筑等3D资产需要大量制作时间，而AI生成的结果能否减少后续修改、顺利接入现有工作流程，直接关系到提效能否兑现。
今年5月底，VAST发布了这一项目的研究预览，其核心思路是将世界状态与画面渲染分开，就比如物体、空间以及交互造成的变化，再根据不同玩家的视角生成对应画面，让多人能够在同一个持续存在的环境中行动。
从这些研发方向来看，GameLook认为，VAST正在同时推进两种与游戏相关的能力，一方面是让开发者更快制作所需资产，另一方面是探索由AI支持、能够持续交互的虚拟环境。
按照本轮融资披露，新增资金将用于3D原生模型和数据能力迭代、训练与推理基础设施扩建，以及产品开发和商业化推进。
这些来自真实项目的答案，将决定AI 3D能够在游戏行业走多远。

title: 欧美游戏圈“再添荒唐事”！《星战》新游爆卖，80%员工却停薪留职
event_sentences: 荒唐的是在游戏发售的前三周，开发团队Bit Reactor就已经进入了“裁员倒计时”，80%的员工被停薪留职，成了待宰的羔羊。
这是继7月《刺客信条：黑旗》重制版巴塞罗那工作室的大规模裁员的余声未却，欧美游戏行业又一桩“卸磨杀驴”的行业丑闻。
8月27日，《零号连队》上线后获得了不小的热度，迅速登顶Steam、PS畅销榜，对于工作室的员工而言未必是一个喜讯，目前这80%的员工未来是去是留，仍旧是未知数。
工作室CEO兼创意总监Greg Foertsch是一位行业老兵，曾在Firaxis Games供职22年，从高级美术一路升至美术总监，亲手参与了《文明》系列、《XCOM：未知敌人》、《XCOM2》、等作品，是现代XCOM重启版的美术掌舵人。
《零号连队》上线后被大量玩家和媒体视作XCOM精神继承者，同时也做出了星战味。
虽然目前官方暂未公布销量，但 依据销售形势来看，GameLook预计游戏销售数量很有可能突破百万套大关。
但恰恰是这样一款品质优秀、市场表现出色的作品，它的开发团队却在游戏上线前干了一件让人看不下去的荒唐事。
据海外Game File记者爆料，Bit Reactor工作室在《零号连队》发售大约三周前，对约80%的员工执行了无薪停薪留职，同时终止了大量外包合约，仅保留少量骨干处理上线后的BUG修复和版本维护。
停薪留职与裁员裁员不同，员工薪资停发但劳动关系名义上得以保留，截至目前工作室对员工回归时间和复薪条件没有任何明确时间表。
Bit Reactor的首款游戏《零号连队》开发周期长达五年，在项目上线前资金已耗尽。
上线前游戏市场表现未知，工作室判断如果销量不及预期，恐怕连工资都发不出来，于是选择用停薪留职的方式压缩成本。
如果上线后卖得不好，这批人实质上就等同被裁；如果卖得好，再视情况召回，把经营风险转嫁给了普通员工。
前高级技术美术（五月离职）Zachariah Scott公开发声：“一边大肆吹捧这款作品的巨大成功，一边掩盖团队早已被停薪的事实，这很荒诞，却已是游戏行业司空见惯的现状。
2026年8月原告方提交的补充法庭文件中，首次书面披露了工作室大部分员工停薪、外包解约的事实。
截至2026年8月中旬，全球游戏业已确认裁掉10618个岗位，覆盖126家公司，另有29家工作室彻底关闭，日均44人失业。
现在员工进退两难，拿不到工资，也没有离职补偿金。
那CEO和CFO理应第一个降薪，这难道不正是他们该负责的范畴吗。
这件事情太荒唐：“一家新工作室在首款作品上线前就要扛五年资金压力，实在疯狂。
从《黑旗》裁员到《零号连队》停薪留职，从Epic千人裁员到29家工作室关门，整个行业正在滑向项目制、短期化、风险转嫁，越来越像电影工业的运作模式，而这恰恰是游戏行业最不想看到的结果。

title: 小红书押注AI小游戏，跟微信抖音抢地盘
event_sentences: 图文社区的AI互动“实验”

但“大事儿”之外，其实也有一些“小事儿”值得关注，就比如，国内头部内容平台不约而同地转向了“小游戏”——B站的叫"Toy"，是一个支持UP主上传测试、小游戏、工具等创意的互动内容发布平台，支持AI辅助生成，像之前风靡一时的“SBTI人格测试”就是范例之一。
抖音的叫“互动空间广场”，用户自制的互动作品涵盖AI互动剧情故事、休闲小游戏，抖音不仅提供了广场，还提供工具，用户可以直接使用字节旗下的AI工具Trae来完成创作，直接浏览效果。
快手也发布了AI互动内容首批创作者招募，点名招募对“互动剧情、AI角色对话、互动轻应用形态”有兴趣的创作者；
简单理解：不联网也能正常使用的纯前端小工具”，不太适合“依赖 AI 接口、实时数据、登录系统、排行榜、云端存档或多人实时互动”的作品。
所以，小工具里多是像性格测试、抽签模拟器、休闲小游戏、本地图片处理器、各类计算器还有番茄钟、日程表这样的作品。
小红书官方推出的vibe coding作品榜Top100榜单估计也是流量分发环节中的一环，我们可以直观看到哪款小工具使用人数多，哪款小工具7天活跃度高，当日新发布的小工具还有单独榜单，可以说是赚足了曝光。
根据榜单来看，休闲小游戏还是在一众测试测评、查询工具、图像创作工具中略胜一筹，Top10中有七名都是休闲游戏。
不过，小工具里的分类也并不是那么准确，就像高居榜二的“理想型测试（阴湿版）”，虽然分类是测试，但就像它介绍的那样，内容偏重“沉浸式情感体验”，测试结果算是其次，包含的meta要素在恋爱游戏里反倒更加常见。
当然了，在测试测评这个赛道，也没多少用户是真的为了科学严谨的测试结果来的，大部分的测试都更像是一种社交名片或安慰剂。
比如“chiikawa角色性格测试”，不管测试结果是吉伊还是乌萨奇，除了发给朋友附送一连串“哈哈哈”以外，也没有太多别的作用了。
并且，就如同现阶段所有内容平台的AI小游戏尝试一般，除了平台自己给的激励以外，小红书的小工具暂时也没有任何商业变现方式。
拥抱AI工具创作者，而非AI
其实小工具并非今天才全面公开，早在8月18日，“科技薯”便宣布，小红书工具已经全量上线。
此前内测期间，只有粉丝量 ≥ 1000的国内注册用户才能发布小工具，每日名额还会限量。
这样的流量增长背后，肯定少不了小红书平台自身的推送逻辑发力，另一方面，8月18日到8月27日左右的近10天时间，或许也能被视为一轮vibe coding产品从开发到发布，再到被二次传播的完整周期。
首批创作者在功能全量开放后涌入，用几小时、几天完成创意上线流程，在不断优化迭代中，积累了用户数据的优质作品获得更大曝光，进入更大的流量池，从而完成社交裂变。
前几个月，AI游戏正声势浩荡的时候，“AI+社交”曾一度成为业界反复提起的热点，也确实有不少类似项目在业内取得了不错声量，比如自然选择的《ELYS》。
简单来说，《ELYS》就是一个AI与人类共存的社交平台，你可以在《ELYS》上创造自己的“AI分身”，“AI分身”会替你社交。
不过，现阶段的AI似乎还无法直接替代人类的社交行为，不少用户都发帖吐槽过AI分身“复读机”、“已读乱回”的问题。
而小红书作为社交媒体平台，走的也是“AI+社交”的大方向，但路径不同。
可以说，小红书完全不追求AI与人类的共存，平台严格限制使用三方工具或脚本（如AI）来运营账号的方式，专项治理AI 伪造人脸、高频同质化 AI 人脸内容。
就像小工具和vibe coding大赛所体现出的态度，小红书选择的是拥抱熟练使用AI工具的人。

title: 上海拟重奖腾网米鹰莉完美，最高或五百万

title: 我玩了一整天暴雪射击新游，感觉很复杂
event_sentences: 就目前软上线的版本而言，活动、好友等部分功能仍未正式开放，我这次游玩时也还不能自由选择模式，只能从系统提供的随机匹配中进入比赛。
今年2月最初开放测试时，游戏只有卢西奥、士兵：76、猎空、雾子、莱因哈特、死神、天使和法老之鹰8名英雄；这一次软上线又加入了布丽吉塔，成为第9名可玩角色。
这次软上线，暴雪又进一步加入英雄等级（Hero Levels）系统。
2018年《暗黑破坏神：不朽》公布后，暴雪联合创始人阿伦·亚德翰就曾表示，公司已经有不少核心开发者在围绕旗下IP制作新的移动游戏，其中既有与外部厂商合作的项目，也有内部自行开发的产品。
按照Newzoo的数据预计，2026年全球游戏市场规模将达到2139亿美元，其中移动游戏贡献1211亿美元，占据整个市场超过一半的收入。
2022年6月上线后，《暗黑破坏神：不朽》只用了不到两个月，就在App Store和Google Play获得超过1亿美元的玩家消费。
2023年11月全球上线之后，《魔兽大作战》最初的表现并不算太差。
游戏本身并非没有得到认可，围绕魔兽角色搭建的即时策略玩法在上线初期收获过不少正面评价。
2022年有报道称，暴雪与网易曾经合作开发一款代号“Neptune”的《魔兽世界》移动端衍生作品。
这款游戏开发时间达到约三年，据报道，网易一度投入超过100人的团队，但项目最终被取消。
此后双方对于取消原因存在不同说法，暴雪也否认双方存在所谓的财务纠纷，但项目本身最终没有面世。
有成功的，有失败的，也有开发数年以后最终没能上线的。

title: 禁AI、高难度，这个挑战赛却涌进20多国1300名创作者
event_sentences: 首先，今年对于MLBB来说是一个比较特殊的时期：从2016年上线至今，MLBB来到了生命周期中的第一个十年。
其次，这是沐瞳首次面向专业创作者举行的挑战赛，比赛的规程、作品都曝光于业内知名的创作者网站上。
在整场比赛里，参赛者不仅需要在两种主题中选择其一，为五名英雄设计一整套系列皮肤，又要提交草图、过程和设计说明，还要考虑设计能否在游戏里实际落地，其规格显然超过了一般面向玩家的征集活动。
在比赛的十周内，整场活动吸引了来自20多个国家和地区的1300余名创作者报名，收到500余件有效作品，赛事页面访问量超过10万。
比如获得了一等奖的作品就是葡萄牙创作者TaissOnAir的《The Heraion Cup》，从它的作品看来，你就能意识到玩家们的热情投注到了一个什么程度。
在许多实际的皮肤设计流程中，除了美型、创意之外，如何落地其实也是幕后设计需要考虑的环节之一，因此《The Heraion Cup》的优势可能正在这里。
MLBB于2016年上线，今年正好是产品的第十个年头。
目前，游戏已经覆盖全球220多个国家和地区，累计注册用户超过15亿，月活跃用户峰值达到了1.1亿。
在Sensor Tower今年1月发布的《State of Mobile 2026》中，MLBB还位列2025年全球手游MAU榜第六名。
继M7在雅加达举行后，下一届M8世界总决赛将首次走进欧洲，落地土耳其伊斯坦布尔。
这样优秀作品既有机会进入游戏，参赛者也可能由玩家或自由创作者，进一步成为沐瞳的合作艺术家乃至正式员工，由此拓开更深的文化内核。
关注AI消息的朋友可能听过类似的说法，对于所有在2021年之后产生的内容，最好都在心里打个问号，因为这之后的内容已经不是过去由人类纯“手搓”而成的了。
尽管这样的说法有些放大AI焦虑的意味，但某种程度上来说，它是对的。
这次MLBB的皮肤设计挑战赛明确禁止了AI生成内容，也是在强调这种理念，由此产生的作品自然可以看出参赛者来自哪里、接触过什么文化、平时喜欢怎样的作品，它们才是给内容真正增添活力的事情。
不过，比赛禁用AI并不意味着沐瞳拒绝AI。
在不同的场景内区分好如何更完善地使用AI，其实表达的主体依然是人。
分布在不同国家的创作者可能继续成为合作艺术家、内容作者，甚至继续加入项目团队。
在2016年前后，当时的手游刚刚超过端游，进入快速扩张的年代；而十年之后，市场环境、玩家审美、硬件渠道和内容标准都已经发生了很大变化，许多曾经流行的产品也早已淡出视野。

title: 给裁员潮下游戏人的15条建议
event_sentences: 几天前，gamescom dev的开幕演讲把一个不太轻松的话题摆到了台前：裁员。
既然裁员潮避无可避，回到具体的问题上，普通从业者还能做些什么？
在科隆游戏展的另一场圆桌中，几名来自招聘、制作和共研等领域的从业者，谈到了如今的用人变化，也分享了他们在小团队、项目制合作和跨行业工作中的经验。
这些经验未必适用于所有人，但至少为即将被裁员、正在经历裁员或已被裁员的从业者提供了一些可以主动尝试的方向，我们从中整理出以下15条建议，可供参考：
一款游戏从立项走到上线，每个阶段需要的人并不相同。
对尚未拥有大量上线项目的人来说，这些能力尤其重要。
求职前，可以主动查看同行和潜在竞争者的资料：他们在哪里工作，参与过哪些上线项目，掌握什么技能，作品集达到了怎样的质量。
重点不在到场打卡，而在持续认识同行，让一次普通交流有机会变成后续合作。
几位自由职业者的客户都来自会议和行业活动中的交流，其中一人在大约六周内签下4名客户，有两次合作源自GDC和gamescom期间的谈话。
不妨提前准备一段简短的自我介绍：做过什么，最擅长哪一块，现在想找什么样的工作或合作。
全球AAA游戏的新增投资已经从2021财年的100亿美元降至上一财年的20亿美元；过去18个月，没有任何一个新立项的3A项目预算超过了1亿美元。
意大利独立游戏《四叶草深渊》由Panik Arcade的两名开发者制作，于2025年9月上线。
不到两个月，官方便宣布销量突破100万份。
近几年远程全职岗位减少较多，相比之下，远程合同工、自由职业和按项目合作的机会反而有所增加。
发布于：北京市

title: 对话创始人：欧美Top 1的XR眼镜，能玩《影之刃零》了？
event_sentences: 这其实是VITURE和《影之刃零》刚刚公布的一次联名合作，眼镜的外观设计贴合游戏的气质， 目前已经全球开启预售，中国则在京东独家预售，未来 会跟 《影之刃零》在10月29日 同步 正式 发 售 。

IDC数据显示，VITURE已连续多个季度保持美国XR眼镜市场出货量第一；2026年Q1，VITURE成为欧美第一出货量XR品牌；去年和《赛博朋克2077》合作的联名眼镜全球限量一万台，发售后很快售罄。
VITURE创始人兼CEO姜公略
2024年的VITURE Pro发布时定价439美元，今年规格更高的VITURE Pro 2已经降到了299美元。
姜公略相信，未来眼镜上还是会出现全新的游戏内容，甚至有些内容只能通过眼镜来体验；VITURE和《赛博朋克2077》《影之刃零》这样的合作，也可能从今天的联名产品，进一步走向针对眼镜打造的专属游戏体验。

title: 加码布局AI产业生态，游族网络2026年上半年营收、净利润双增
event_sentences: 8月27日晚，游族网络发布2026年半年度报告。
公司以AI推动经营效能全面提升，通过全球市场的长线深耕及小游戏赛道拓展，实现整体业绩稳健增长； 公司还持续推进AI生态布局，构筑未来长效发展新动能。
在“616少年节”期间，公司二十余款游戏面向全球玩家发布特别福利活动，有效拉动用户活跃度与营收增长。
此外，SLG手游《Zomline Survival》已启动海外公测。
游族网络将AI作为驱动经营管理及业务变革的核心抓手，通过工具创新、机制保障等多维度协同发力，有效实现经营效能提升。
游族网络自研并在内部推出了多个AI平台及工具：YOOZOO.AI聚合平台已接入数十个大模型，支持数百个业务场景，覆盖全球化游戏研运全链路工作需求；AI广告素材创作平台打通从创意构思到视频生成的全链路生产流程；游戏创作平台YOOSpark实现“自然语言对话让AI做游戏”，支持零基础游戏创作；视觉创作工具YOOLab游族万象画布以高自由度、可视化的图文与视频生成能力串联AI创作全链路。

凭借领先的AI布局、规模化落地成果与产业生态建设能力，公司成功获评《2026游戏产业AI发展报告》“AI布局代表性企业”。

title: 游戏爆卖2000万份，CEO却说：我们不想扩张，只想做150人的小团队
event_sentences: 2024年2月，瑞典独立工作室Arrowhead Game Studios凭借《绝地潜兵2》一跃成为行业焦点。
这款由俯视角射击转型为第三人称合作射击的作品， 发售后三天内销量突破百万份，十天内在Steam平台达成超过33万同时在线玩家峰值， 一度超越多款同期3A级即时服务大作。
截至2026年，行业分析机构Alinea估算其累计销量已超过2000万份，总收入逾7亿美元； 该作亦在TGA 2024中摘得“最佳多人游戏”与“最佳持续运营游戏”两项殊荣。
工作室CEO Shams Jorjani在德国科隆展接受GamesBeat专访时透露， 团队规模在游戏发售时有110人，希望未来长期控制在150人以内。
在此次采访中，Jorjani亦坦率分享了爆款之后的压力管理、对增长边界的克制思考、对行业商业模式多样性的担忧、对AI技术秉持的务实态度，以及如何迎战即将到来的《GTA VI》市场巨浪。
而且，虽然我们现在很成功，但很多公司正是因为成功时扩张太快、决策失误，最终不得不裁员，我们不想重蹈覆辙。
以Supercell 为例，他们曾长期坚持“不扩张”的原则，把团队人数控制在250人以内，比如《部落冲突》的运营团队只有15人左右。
但后来他们发现，当服务型游戏赚钱时，运营团队需要变得非常庞大，甚至超过最初的设计团队，这是他们不得不接受的现实。
Jorjani： 我对Supercell一直很关注。

title: The Big Picture: What you need to know about the ongoing games industry reset
event_sentences: Satvat is best-known for founding the ASGC , which provides help and advice for job seekers, and in a wide-ranging speech, he dove into the data behind the huge numbers of games industry layoffs, the shift of jobs to different regions, the concentration of revenue among just a few key companies, the changing nature of employment and games, and how the industry needs to adapt to face the current crisis.

He started with the bad news. Back in December, Satvat told GamesIndustry.biz that he expected around 7,500 redundancies across the industry in 2026 , down from the roughly 9,200 in 2025. Following the huge waves of redundancies this year, Satvat has now revised that prediction to 14,666, not far off from the 2024 peak of 15,631. As of August 11, there have already been around 10,140 announced layoffs this year – more than for the whole of 2025.

Satvat cited "very convincing" research from the Game Industry Coffee Chat (GICC) group indicating that roughly 750,000 people are employed directly or indirectly in the games industry, much higher than typically reported figures. "The reason this often gets very undercounted in my opinion is people don't understand the extent of employment in China," explained Satvat.

The upshot is that "even with all these cuts that have been going on," said Satvat, "the industry is actually net positive in terms of employees from 2022 until now." It's only a small growth of less than 1%, but it is growth nonetheless. (Pre-2022, however, the industry saw explosive growth, adding around 150,000 net jobs over the five years from 2017.)
The research firm's report also predicts that the handheld PC sold 1.6 million units during 2022

What's happened over the past five years is a geographic transition. "Head count moving from basically North America to basically anywhere else," Satvat said, with the move motivated not just by labour costs but also things like "government incentives and talent availability."

Satvat said that over two-thirds of the layoffs he has been tracking have occurred in North America, pegging the total losses at 25,000 roles amounting to 15% of the workforce. California was hit hardest; in one period of 12-18 months, over 50% of overall layoffs were in that state.

Other regions, meanwhile, have seen a net gain of jobs. Asia Pacific (APAC) saw the number of available jobs increase by 10%, driven by 12% growth within China. The number of roles in Europe, meanwhile, has "basically stayed flat," Satvat said.
Uneven revenue spread

One thing that's confusing is why so many layoffs are happening at a time when the games industry is experiencing continued growth. The reason, says Satvat, is that growth is confined to a decreasing number of titles. "You have 50, 60% of the revenue being distributed to just the top 20 games."
A small percentage of games take the lion's share of revenue | Image credit: Amir Satvat

On mobile it's increasingly difficult to acquire users, meaning the sector is now focused on monetization of existing players - while on PC, only 79 titles account for 80% of play time. "So the top line numbers look good, but … the numbers are much tougher when you go beneath the surface."
Former Sony Worldwide Studios head Shawn Layden and analysts Mat Piscatella and Piers Harding-Rolls look ahead to the future of the games industry

Satvat listed 21 pressures the games industry is facing, including post-pandemic overhiring, changing player habits, longer development cycles, and rising production costs. But the two he worries about the most are discoverability pressure and AI uncertainty, because "to the best of my knowledge, no person has some master plan of how to have a solution to either of those two things, and not solving those two things could be a sinker that invalidates everything else I'm about to talk about."
However, he said that above everything else, the geographic transition we're experiencing is "the biggest driver of change in the industry."

Yet the chances of these new graduates with no prior games experience finding entry-level jobs are tiny. "There's a 4% chance of obtaining employment in games over a 12 month period of time," said Satvat. He added that overall, across the world, there were roughly five job seekers for every annual hire. But that ratio rises to 11:1 in North America.

"There's also an interesting squeeze that's been going on in terms of seniority," said Satvat. "The average credentials that jobs are asking for, for the same job, have gone up by three years. And this further creates a squeeze down on early career candidates, because now if they're looking at roles that traditionally would be no experience, or one or two years, and they can ask for and get candidates who have three to four years experience, because people are looking for work."

In addition, there seem to be fewer roles available for senior developers. "My data suggests that when you get to the age of 50 or equivalent experience, you go back down to 4-5% again. And so what's happening is we have this kind of odd sweet spot, where people who are basically between early experience and up to, like, 15, 20 years [of experience] are very, very employable. But people who start falling outside those ends are having a great deal of trouble."

In terms of the types of jobs companies are hiring for, Satvat said that the traditional "big four" categories – which typically account for around 70% of open roles – are art and animation, engineering, production and project management, and game design. But recently, game design has fallen out of the big four, to be replaced by marketing. In addition, the relative share of open roles in business intelligence, data, and analytics has increased, while writing and narrative, QA, and recruiting have declined in terms of the overall share of open roles.

Getting hired increasingly depends on networking and personal connections. "You are 20x plus more likely to get a job these days if you have any connection to the hiring manager or the recruiter versus not," said Satvat. He also encouraged job hunters to seek out work experience. "If you can just get one to two years of work experience, statistically, your odds over 12 months of getting another games role if you're unemployed jumps from 4% to 30%."

Satvat went on to outline a number of structural shifts that the video game industry is currently undergoing. First of all, he said that revenue growth in the console sector is coming "more and more from an engagement with existing customers" through things like premium releases and higher-priced subscription tiers, rather than an increase in the number of players. And audience growth will be put under further pressure by increased hardware prices.

He suggests the traditional model of driving people towards consoles with exclusive releases and improved graphics will "soften", and the focus will instead be about making games more accessible, "because a lot of people just aren't going to be able to afford the hardware."

The market in China, meanwhile, is growing at an astonishing rate: "The numbers are just mind boggling." 42% of global PC revenue growth came from China, while minigames on the Chinese social media platform WeChat have more than 500 million monthly active users. "And now because more and more people in China are going to college, each year we can comfortably expect 10 million plus people who are going to have computers."

On the one hand, he said, the Chinese market offers a market opportunity for developers outside China, because the "taste for games in China [is] not that different from the taste [in] other places." But on the other hand, Chinese developers will provide more competition globally, "because God, when you go over there and you see the volume and the number of studios… And I think in most cases, we have all underestimated how transformative and impactful that's going to be over the next few years."

In terms of where growth opportunities lay, Satvat pointed towards large user-generated content (UGC) platforms like Roblox and UEFN, but also sounded a note of caution that the "revenue opportunities on those platforms [are] concentrated in the hands of a very small number of people."

Competition is getting ever tougher: the number of new Steam releases reached around 12,000 in H1 2026, up 19% year on year. However, Satvat emphasised not to put too much store in those numbers, like the headline of around 20,000 games being released on Steam in 2025. "If you actually pick that number apart, only 3% of those games, about 600, have a hundred or more peak CCU," he said. In other words, the real level of competition is lower than it seems at first glance.
Investment has slid sharply since 2021 | Image credit: Amir Satvat

Meanwhile, the funding landscape looks more bleak. Satvat pointed to the collapse in global games start-up funding from $9.9 billion in 2021 to just $2 billion in 2023, and a similar drop in private equity and venture capital funding from $12.1 billion to $2.7 billion. Partly, this decline could be about misalignment. "I think most investment vehicles and games don't mix," said Satvat, noting that games rarely deliver predictable outcomes or giant returns.

Now, those conversations are out in the open (like our chat with Fuse Games CEO Matt Webster on the use of exdev on Star Wars: Galactic Racer ), and Satvat sees it in the data. When he began tracking job roles in 2022, around half of the jobs were in AAA; that has now shrunk to below one-third. Meanwhile, jobs in external development and contracting have risen to make up roughly 10-15% of open roles.

The remaining open roles are made up of indies, smaller players, tools and services – and Satvat said the biggest opportunities lie in the middle ground between solo indies and global giants, as the power base in gaming shifts.

"People often say to me, Amir, when are we going to go back to normal?" Satvat said. "I don't think, unfortunately, we're going back to normal. I think we're evolving to something else, and what that something else is hasn't been decided yet."

He also thinks firms need to start engaging players at the very start of development. "Let's get rid of this idea, which is a little bit antiquated, that you have to keep this game behind the curtain," he said. "Community access, engagement and feedback is becoming much more important than ever before."

He advocated for more flexible pricing ("so much more of the action these days is in $30 or less, $10 or less") and improved job conditions: "We need to freaking treat game workers better." He particularly cited callous offboarding processes and lack of ongoing development, which he said is driving talented people out of video games. "I estimate 120,000 years of games experience have already permanently left the industry since I started tracking things in 2022. If we want to stop that bleeding out, that's recommendation number one."

He wants to see dramatic changes to video games education programs, too, not only giving candidates upfront information about their slim chances of landing a job in games, but also providing them with training that goes beyond the games industry. More than 60% of the people that ASGC helped this year found work outside of games.

Importantly, Satvat sees a shift to smaller teams with tighter budgets as a "big part of the solution" to the current crisis, where games directly target a niche rather than simply aiming for the most popular genres. "That starts with a small team really thinking about the customers, being increasingly comfortable with exdev and contracting."
Satvat highlighted two scenarios that could happen, but that we should aim to avoid

He posited two less-desirable outcomes. "One is kind of extraction, where everything that's mature market, that's IP, gets bought by financial players, gets hauled out, and is just run for [...] extractive revenue of what's left, and [there's] more and more ownership concentration.

"The other one, for lack of a better term, I call 'small ball', which is [where] everything goes kind of really hard to the edge of UGC, and maybe because of AI and other factors, everyone is just running lots of really small entities and that doesn't have a lot of concentration. It makes things even worse than they are for people wanting to find an opportunity to build teams [and] to have continuity."

That scenario involves redefining success, whereby rather than needing millions of sales, companies can be profitable at much lower figures thanks to keeping a tight focus on development costs. "And if we went back to having that disciplined, smaller, steadier, and healthier ecosystem, I don't think that would be such a bad thing, and it could set us up for where we want the industry to go in the future."

Supercell clarified that its games will "continue as normal" as the deal goes through, and that the "team remains dedicated to the community that has made Merge Mansion their own for years."

title: "Sometimes you need fresh perspectives" – How external development helped Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis
event_sentences: A hands-off demonstration of Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis at Gamescom last week showed that the game is far from a simple remaster of the 1996 original; it's a complete reworking of Lara Croft's first adventure.

Crystal Dynamics has handed over the development reins to Polish studio Flying Wild Hog , which has added much to the Tomb Raider formula. Notably, the first-aid kits are gone, replaced by Lara crafting health-giving tinctures and stat-boosting meals from collectable ingredients. Lara now also has a skill tree: the demo showed the use of skill points to boost the range of Lara's iconic dual pistols.

At a round-table Q&A after the demo, Raul Siqueira, game director at Crystal Dynamics, and Flying Wild Hog art director Arek Tomaszewski shed light on how the external development partnership worked, the studios' relationship with Amazon, and why we won't be seeing the return of tank controls in Legacy of Atlantis when it launches on February 12.

"We are really good at breaking down the invisible walls that we can build between studios during development," he says. "It became very clear when we first started talking to each other that both studios saw game development in the same way. We were very good about being honest about what's needed and how we want to do it. It was just one of those things that came very naturally.
The Gamescom demo showcased the Sword of Damocles area | Image credit: Crystal Dynamics/Flying Wild Hog/Amazon Game Studios

"Obviously, Crystal comes from a background of a lot of Tomb Raider games, and there's a lot of history here, but sometimes you need fresh perspectives. Sometimes you need someone new to come in and look at what you have so you can create something unique. I feel like that collaboration has been one of the best parts of this project."

Of course, Flying Wild Hog isn't the only relationship that Crystal Dynamics is having to manage with Legacy of Atlantis. Tech and retail giant Amazon is publishing both this project and the upcoming Tomb Raider: Catalyst , as well as producing a TV series based on the IP starring Sophie Turner .
Siqueira says that his studio is working "pretty closely" with Amazon on all fronts,

"We share a commitment to the franchise and to the character that goes past the walls of the studio and beyond," he says. "We do have an internal franchise team at Crystal Dynamics. They're masterminds, responsible people who have worked on the franchise for 20-plus years. Then they're engaged across the board in all projects. There's a great collaboration between everyone."

At the outset, the team replayed the 1996 original as well as the 2007 remake, Tomb Raider: Anniversary, which emphasised how the memory can play tricks. "We all have that memory of what that game looks like in our brain, and then we play it, and we're like, 'Ah, that's different'," says Siqueira. "And in doing so, we were able to identify, OK, what are some of the key moments, key locations, things that we have to preserve, that have to stay exactly as they are, then where can we kind of colour outside the lines?"
The bats have been made more of a significant enemy in Legacy of Atlantis | Image credit: Crystal Dynamics/Flying Wild Hog/Amazon Game Studios

"The control scheme has been adapted to fit the modern audience," Siqueira says. "Of course, the original games are always available to you: We just did Tomb Raider 1 Remastered. If you want to go back to tank controls, I applaud your enthusiasm. I tried it many times, and man, it's hard."

When it was first revealed, Legacy of Atlantis made its debut alongside Tomb Raider: Catalyst, where the latter is a sequel set years after the events of 2008's Tomb Raider: Underworld . Asked how much synergy there is between the two projects, Siqueira says that there is "definitely collaboration" between the two games, and that there are not multiple versions of the main character.
Legacy of Atlantis was originally scheduled to release in 2026, but earlier this year it was pushed back to February 2027 | Image credit: Crystal Dynamics/Flying Wild Hog/Amazon Game Studios

"Obviously, we are making the games together," he says. "However, it is very important for us to distinguish that Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis is completely its own project and we are making sure that we are staying faithful to the original game. When it comes to specifics of where Lara is in her journey moving forward, we want to be respectful to both the games that came before and the games that came after. The Lara you see here is the same Lara from the Survivor era [Tomb Raider 2013, Rise of the Tomb Raider, and Shadow of the Tomb Raider, which tell Lara's origin story], and it will be the same Lara in our projects moving forward."
Disclosure: Alex Forbes-Calvin has previously worked with Crystal Dynamics on the book Chronicles of the Tomb Raider.

title: Aggro Crab launches publishing label to splash that Peak cash
event_sentences: The studio wants to support 'intense, stylized games with an attitude' - but isn't interested in 'generative AI slop.'

Peak and Another Crab's Treasure developer Aggro Crab has launched a publishing label and is actively soliciting submissions from teams building video games that are, in its own words, "absolute gas."

Aggro Crab Presents will support projects that require $500,000 or less to launch within two years. The company said it wants to nurture "intense, stylized games with an attitude" but isn't locked into any specific genres.
Crucially, Aggro Crab head of publishing Corey Warning said the team has no interest in publishing titles that leverage "generative AI slop."
The new initiative has been made possible thanks to the success of social climber, Peak , which has topped 20 million players worldwide since launching in June 2025.
Related: Nexus Mods is acquiring database and analytics site SteamDB

Aggro Crab will take full advantage of its social media reach and existing audience to promote its publishing slate. It emphasised that Aggro Crab Presents is operated by the same people responsible for developing, vibe-checking, and playtesting the studio's own titles. This isn't a spinoff, but rather an extension of Aggro Crab's existing responsibilities.

"We want game devs who work with us to know that the same care and attention is going into promoting their game as any title Aggro Crab develops," said the studio. "We also want to publish games that we, the developers at Aggro Crab, are personally passionate about! We believe that enthusiasm for a project shines through on all levels, and so when we sign a game, it’s because we wanna be those devs' biggest fans."
Providing some sense of what publishing terms developers can expect, Aggro Crab said its contract includes some "base terms" and adjustable agreements that can be tailored to different projects.

Aggro Crab is also committed to implementing flexible milestones. "We want developers to have a solid understanding of their game’s scope and timeline before we sign, but we also understand that sometimes things just need to change (we’ve been there, believe me…)," wrote the studio. "If we need to adjust deliverables, split up payments, add or push a milestone, within reason, we can likely make it work. We believe firmly that trust in a publishing partnership should be a two-way street."

In addition, the company is shunning 100 percent recoup and insisted that "revenue needs to be flowing back towards the developers so they can continue to support themselves and the game after launch."
"We also don’t hold the final payment for the game’s release date milestone: devs need that money to finish the game," added the studio.

title: Report: Savvy Games Group CEO Brian Ward departs company
event_sentences: 'As Savvy embarks on its next period of transformational growth, this is the right time for new leadership for that evolution.'

Saudi Arabian video game conglomerate Savvy Games Group appears to be experiencing a change in leadership. That's according to a report from Bloomberg News , which states that CEO Brian Ward is stepping down from his position.

Ward apparently announced the news to Savvy employees in a message stating that it is "the right time for new leadership" as it "embarks on its next period of transformational growth." He is apparently being temporarily replaced by Turqi Alnowaiser, deputy governor of Savvy Game Group's parent organization: the government-owned Saudi Arabia Public Investment fund (PIF). Alnowaiser also is the head of the PIF's international investments division.

Ward became CEO of Savvy Games Group in 2021 and oversaw a $37.8 billion spree of international investments and acquisitions in game companies large and small. During his time as CEO, Savvy acquired significant stakes in companies like Embracer Group , Take-Two Entertainment , and Nintendo . Its most significant acquisitions include its $4.9 billion purchase of mobile developer Scopely and its $3.5 billion acquisition of Pokémon Go developer Niantic .
Related: Nexus Mods is acquiring database and analytics site SteamDB

As those investments progressed, industry professionals expressed growing concern about the PIF's ownership of Savvy, which links the conglomerate to the Saudi government. Those concerns were echoed by members of the US Congress after the PIF led a joint $55 billion buyout of Battlefield and The Sims developer Electronic Arts (EA) that did not directly involve Savvy itself.

However, the buyout of EA may be driving difficult questions inside Savvy Games Group. Sources speaking to Bloomberg say the purchase of EA has raised concern over "how the two giant Saudi-owned video-game businesses will be run."

在西方国家，我们会质疑（使用）AI是否符合伦理，公司是否被允许使用数据训练AI模型，以及我们是否应当基于思想或艺术立场予以抵制。
他们的想法与IT从业者很相似：几乎所有程序员都张开双臂拥抱AI，没有任何重大道德顾虑，甚至连一丝疑虑都没有。
“当AI被引入游戏开发流程时，西方游戏开发者往往会觉得他们面临着一场生存危机。
作为一名艺术家，我能理解这种感受：我希望我的作品能够在艺术层面让人们产生共鸣，AI却会将它异化成功能性的工具。
因此，西方开发者接受AI的速度可能稍慢一些，但最终还是会接受的。
”乔尔贾尼指出，“游戏开发周期依然漫长，市场正在不断变化，为了减少风险，厂商在做出任何立项决策前必须非常谨慎。
例如，如果‘百战天虫’（Worms）系列新作与另外10款游戏同时发布，某些玩家可能会出于对这个经典系列的了解而优先选择它。
有数据显示，Steam用户将一半的游玩时间都投入了那些问世已经超过18个月的游戏。
乔尔贾尼补充：“我们的运气还算不错，因为我们属于极少数通过单个IP取得突破，并在行业内站稳脚跟的幸运儿之一。
在多人合作射击游戏的细分市场，《绝地潜兵》既极具辨识度，又显得独树一帜。
按照乔尔贾尼的说法，拳头、Supercell等公司常常同时开发多款游戏，一旦某款游戏爆火，玩家就会忘记那些公司曾经开发的其他几款游戏。
许多独立开发者喜欢发布游戏的GIF动图，如果玩家反响热烈，他们就知道自己走对了路。
这位CEO透露，箭头还从手游厂商的惯用做法中吸取了灵感：手游厂商经常向玩家展示不同的游戏概念（通常以广告形式），然后观察哪些概念的效果最好。
在参与试玩的所有玩家中，我们会重点关注既喜欢《绝地潜兵》和这款新游戏，又对外星人感兴趣的那群人……通过在开发初期组织试玩，我们能尽早知道游戏究竟能否吸引这一特定群体，而不必等到两年后再开展大规模玩家测试。

title: 2026年中，写在国内游戏投资回暖以后
event_sentences: 两个月前，演语科技 （LibTV/LoveArt/LiblibAI） 宣布完成近$3亿的B+轮， 投后估值$20亿，紧接着就开融$30亿轮次 。
同一时期，市场传言阿里出售游戏业务，报价70—90亿人民币，最近尘埃落定，官宣信宸资本敲定了收购灵犀，价格约$15亿。
外界估计灵犀年流水$10-15亿，利润$2-3亿，静态看PS/PE估值实在不贵；演语披露的ARR是近$3亿，也不好说是不是月流水×12，主打一个未来可期。
同样是科技与创作， AIGC如火如荼地卖增长预期，卖下一轮和二级市场更大的买家（会赢的）；游戏卖的是实打实的现金流，却伴随“老产品还能活多久”，“下一个项目能不能爆”，和“最后究竟能卖给谁”的三连问号。
（还得感谢AI）
据媒体统计，26年H1国内发生了约50起游戏行业的投融资事件，即使按“初创融资”、“少数股权”、“纯游戏研发”这样较为严格的口径，有公开信息披露的投资也有约20起，加之水下案例，不算热闹，但也并非前两年行业低谷可比。
最近一年IDG接连投了 金韬 和 李凯明 ，这两位过去十年帮助网易创造了上百亿甚至数百亿流水的顶级制作人，也不过拿了千万美元级的资金。
再往前，big name基金出手可能要追溯到24年IDG投祖龙明星制作人赵同同 （梦幻诛仙/龙族幻想） ，23年红衫/高榕/monolith投资前巨人CEO吴萌 （球球大作战人） 创业。
自腾讯字节争投游戏落幕后，头部VC已经实质上排除了游戏领域的投资，名义上还会看，但其实就是只投履历最顶 （或者说累计流水） 的人，用更高的胜率，对冲不划算的赔率。
本文写作期间，Pilot Ventures的合伙人Yuki也发布了一期嘉宾播客 （也是Justin老板主理的，小宇宙搜索「Just ing | 照见工作与生活」） ，我简单截一节show notes，可以一窥他们的投资哲学：
研发需要发行能力，资方需要产品管线， 股权既是合作的 诚意订金 ，也是避免只共苦不同甘的 长期绑定 。
另一方面，从业务协同的角度，海外演化出一种新的项目投资 （Project Financing） 玩法， UA Funding ，即机构专门提供 买量资金 ，帮助已经验证ROI但无法放大增长的产品，解决 正利润 与 负现金流 之间的gap。
VC、发行方、数据/增长平台，都在试水这种方式，甚至发展出专业的UA Funding平台如PvX Patners 。
长青产品 不只虹吸占着流水，也如参天大树，上，遮蔽阳光， 占着用户的时间和社交关系 ；下，盘根错节， 汲取用户的沉没成本和情感积累 。
如果立项注定小而美，它可能是一款好作品，也可能是一门不错的生意，但 撑不起投资人理想中的回报 。
做项目与做公司，本来就是 两件事情 ，更需要 三种角色 —— 制作人、CEO和股东 。
制作人要判断体验、内容和团队；CEO要管组织、现金流与商业合作；股东还要考虑治理、融资与退出。
少数股权融资最隐蔽的成本，正是 持续抽走主创最稀缺的注意力 。
事实上，往往沉浸于创作、积累于创作的艺术家，就不太具备完整经营管理与连续融资的能力。
制作人与核心骨干整体入职大厂，尽量保留原有建制，带着过去积累的品类能力和磨合经验，在内部重新立项。
告别估值和下一轮融资，项目进入 预算、HC与Greenlight体系 ，按产品节点而非资本历程推进。
外部团队整建制引进，过去二十年各家大厂反复做过， 这条路从来不新 ；只是创业 融资宽松 时，有梦自可以去追，也有充足的资金和机会鼓励大家“出来混”。
对希望建立长期品牌，或者坚持独立文化与公司控制权的团队， 少数股权融资依然是更合适的路 。
但现实更常见的是，团队进来后建制被拆，中台从支持变成掣肘，制作人从融资路演换成内部层层汇报。
它能减少融资和生存压力，给项目更多验证空间；创意成不成立、玩家买不买单，最后仍由作品回答。

title: “MMORPG早就不行了”是事实，还是我们从未做出过像样的尝试？
event_sentences: 但事实证明并不是这样，于是从2020年黑猴第一次亮相往后，陆续有厂商开始立项3A，包括烛龙的古剑、网易的归唐等等。
本文并不是一个立项说明书或者一个BP文案，我只是想阐述我理想中的MMORPG，也许我的想法有不切实际的地方，但不失为一篇抛砖引玉的文章。
但最终这些画面上的成本还是要玩家来买单，逼肝逼氪的内容陆续上线，KPI需求步步紧逼，如果你是免费玩家，就要承受付费玩家的氪金的威压，或者逼肝的内容把你抓回来保持在线。
经典的赛季通行证设计，某个道具只有这个赛季有，如果这个赛季你不打，它就成了绝版物品，这会极大的触发人类的稀缺心理从而迫使你每天上线肝游戏，然而你肝了很久拿到的这些所谓绝版物品只不过是开发商人为定义的一坨数字垃圾，而且还有可能是随手设计的。

有了这个概念基础之后，其实就可以预言一件事，那就是由于AI的发展、游戏引擎技术的发展，未来做游戏会变得越来越简单，游戏的数量会越来越多，这些游戏就像一个非常细密的网一样，将整个用户市场分割为大大小小的各个圈层，就拿二游来说，少前、明日方舟、原神等这些老牌二游有一批自己的用户，但后续的新增二游也不少，于是每个手游能够获得的用户注意力就会下降，虽然总的用户数量不变，但每个二游的用户群都会被分割的更小，这也就意味着维持社交信用的难度会变得更大。
有了这个前提，可以谈谈基于点卡的收费制度的一个时代性优势，前面说了，就是它其实并不过分的依赖游戏的用户群规模，因为它的营收源自于每个用户，平等地看待所有的用户，这就使得官方可以不用出一些逼氪的数值性强化内容导致游戏过早的开始面临运维压力。

title: The Witcher Remake Is Waiting On The Witcher 4 To Continue Development
event_sentences: CD Projekt has confirmed to GameSpot that The Witcher Remake from Fool’s Theory is currently on the back burner as the studio works on The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt’s Songs of the Past expansion and assists with the development of The Witcher 4.

"Fool's Theory team is focused mainly on the development of Witcher 3: Songs of the Past, while a relatively small part of their team is supporting the development of The Witcher 4. As we have previously announced, the development on The Witcher Remake has been temporarily integrated with The Witcher 4 due to production process dependencies. As The Witcher Remake will be built on the foundation laid by The Witcher 4, we need to have the necessary assets, tools, and pipelines ready for efficient development."

We first noticed something was up with The Witcher Remake when joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski mentioned roadblocks for the project in an interview with The Game Business . “We started a collaboration with Fool’s Theory. They were supposed to work on The Witcher 1 [remake], but we realized that needed a bit more time because of certain technology dependencies with The Witcher 4,” Nowakowski revealed.

CD Projekt at large is transitioning from using its proprietary RED Engine for all its games to Unreal Engine . The Witcher 4 will set the standard for what a Witcher game in Unreal Engine looks like, and it appears that The Witcher 1’s remake ( announced in 2022 ) got caught up in that technology shift.

Now, Fool’s Theory is the primary developer of The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt’s upcoming Songs of the Past expansion, which was unveiled at Gamescom, and is helping create The Witcher 4. Once those are complete, work on The Witcher Remake can ramp up again.

Previous statements Nowakowski made in conversations with investors support his latest comments to The Game Business and GameSpot. In its Q3 2024 earnings report Q&A, Nowakowski said that “work is progressing” on the remake, but in the Q&A reflecting on the entire 2024 fiscal year , Nowakowski’s tone on the project changed. He explained that the remake’s development had been integrated with The Witcher 4’s.

“Due to production process dependencies - among others related to assets and technology - we have decided to temporarily integrate its development with ongoing work on The Witcher 4,” he said. “As a result, a small portion of The Fool's Theory team is currently supporting The Witcher 4 team. Our goal is to have the necessary assets, tools, and pipelines ready for more efficient development of The Witcher Remake.”

The Witcher 1’s remake does not have a release window at this time, but from Nowakowski's comments, it seems likely it won’t arrive until after The Witcher 3 Remastered later this month, Songs of the Past in 2027, and The Witcher 4 in 2028.

title: Releasing Cyberpunk 2077 In Its Poor State “Was For Sure Wrong,” CD Projekt Admits
event_sentences: CD Projekt Red's RPG Cyberpunk 2077 infamously launched in December 2020 in such a poor technical state that Sony took the rare move to remove it from the PlayStation Store. Thousands of people refunded the game . CD Projekt joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski has now reflected on this, saying it "was for sure wrong" to launch the game in that state, but he pushed back against the theory that the studio did so to appease investors who wanted to see financial returns.

Speaking to The Game Business , Nowakowski said COVID "was a factor" in the game's rough state at launch, because "the team was getting exhausted in a different way." He admitted there were "people outside telling us we should launch," and fans lobbied for this as well. The developers themselves also "wanted to push it out the door" because the ongoing development was "really tiring."
Looking back on it, now with the benefit of hindsight, Nowakowski said, "The decision to launch was for sure wrong, period. There is no denying it."
That being said, Nowakowski said, "There were no magical investors telling us, 'You have to get this out.'" Instead, he said, "It was much more complicated and psychological."

CD Projekt's fiscal years follow the calendar and end on December 31. Cyberpunk 2077 was released on December 10 in 2020, and this timing led people to wonder if the developer put the game out then instead of delaying to 2021 to meet the fiscal deadline. There is, after all, precedent for game developers pushing games out the door in a rough state to hit certain fiscal deadlines.

Cyberpunk 2077 might have released in a rough technical state, but it was a smashing success at launch commercially. The game sold nearly 14 million copies right out of the gate, which made it one of the most successful RPG releases in the history of video games . Given that success, CD Projekt Red executives got multimillion-dollar bonus payouts , while developers also took home big bonus payouts related to the game's huge success in sales.

Following Cyberpunk 2077's rough launch, CD Projekt Red steadily supported the game with numerous updates and improvements over the years, culminating with a massive, game-changing 2.0 update in 2023 alongside the Phantom Liberty expansion. Today, the game has sold more than 40 million copies .
In other news about Cyberpunk 2077, Microsoft just announced that the game is leaving Xbox Game Pass soon .

Given the huge commercial success of Cyberpunk 2077, it only makes sense that CD Projekt is now making Cyberpunk 2, but it is likely still years away from release . On the more immediate horizon is The Witcher 3: Remastered this year , The Witcher 3's new Songs of the Past expansion in 2027 , and then The Witcher 4 in 2028. Fans hoping to play The Witcher 1's remake might want to get comfortable .

title: Sony To Pay Out Nearly $8 Million In Class-Action Settlement Over Game Prices
event_sentences: Sony is set to pay out nearly $8 million to PlayStation customers as part of a settlement regarding digital game prices. The settlement ( via IGN ) comes after Sony's motion to dismiss the lawsuit was denied, and settlement class members across a more-than-four-year period are potentially eligible for a payment.

The lawsuit, originally filed back in 2024 , alleged that Sony established a monopoly over PlayStation Store prices by making publishers "cede control over the final price to Sony" and that Sony "eliminated the last vestiges of price competition when it stopped allowing outside retailers to sell digital download codes that could be redeemed on the PlayStation Store."

Sony is not agreeing to wrongdoing as part of the settlement, and will be avoiding a civil trial if the terms are agreed upon by the court. Once that happens, the claims against Sony will be dismissed "with prejudice," meaning another lawsuit on the subject cannot be filed.

title: Square Enix Shares Jumped On Buyout Rumors, But The Company Says It’s Not Happening
event_sentences: Following a report that Square Enix was potentially exploring going private, the company behind hit franchises like Final Fantasy has released a statement denying the claims. Japanese business magazine Sentaku originally reported that Square Enix was exploring this possibility and that foreign investment funds were rumored to be interested in a deal, which saw Square Enix's stock rise by 7%.

"The September issue of the monthly magazine Sentaku carried a report regarding the possibility of Square Enix. (the Company) going private," Square Enix wrote in a press release. "However, this information was not announced by the Company. No consideration is currently being given within the Company to taking the Company private."

Even if Square Enix were to change its mind, buying back all shares wouldn't be cheap. Depending on daily stock fluctuations on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Square Enix has a Market Capitalization of roughly $6.67 billion to $6.82 billion. While that's pretty big, Square Enix still pales in comparison to the market valuations of its fellow Japanese gaming giants, Nintendo ($64 billion) and Capcom ($11.33 billion). Where the company stands out is that it has a stable revenue base, and recent financial overhauls have improved its capital efficiency.

Square Enix is also more than just a video game developer and publisher, as it also publishes manga magazines and graphic novels under its Gangan Comics imprint, operates arcade franchises under the Taito Corporation banner, and it has a massive merchandising arm. Looking ahead, Square Enix has plenty of games in the pipeline, including the upcoming releases of Final Fantasy Resonance and Final Fantasy 7 Revelation .

That would make it a lucrative prospect for an offer to go private, as seen in the case of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund--alongside Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner’s private equity firm Affinity Partners and investment company Silver Lake--taking ownership of Electronic Arts last month , concluding a $55 billion deal.
Unfortunately, this takeover has left EA saddled with billions in debt , and it's feared that mass layoffs will follow as the company aims to cut costs.

title: Sony Warns PlayStation Customers Against Harassing Support Staff Amid Disc Backlash
event_sentences: Sony's decision to kill off PlayStation game discs has been met with almost universal disdain since it was first announced, and it looks like its employees have been caught in the crossfire. Just about every Sony announcement or social media post is met with calls for it to reverse its decision, and Sony Japan has instituted a new anti-harassment policy to protect the customer service employees who have had to deal with a vocal contingent of dissatisfied consumers.

These changes also align with new workplace laws in Japan that will take effect later this year. "Similar to other companies in Japan, Sony Interactive Entertainment has published its policy in compliance with a new law taking effect on October 1, which requires employers in Japan to implement measures to address customer harassment," Sony said in response to GameSpot.

While customer service workers are currently dealing with backlash over Sony's decision to focus on an all-digital future, the company has also been criticized for several more recent actions. Sony responded to a class action lawsuit in which it was accused of not clearly informing consumers that its digital store sells game licenses, not full games. Various publishers have also accused Sony of anti-competitive moves and of working toward creating a monopoly through its digital storefront. Sony will pay out nearly $8 million to PlayStation customers as part of a settlement over digital game prices.

title: Witcher 4 Dev “Not Worried” About Future Of Consoles Despite Rising Costs
event_sentences: CD Projekt joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski is "not worried" about the future of consoles, despite rising costs that could impact growth in the sector .

Speaking to The Game Business , Nowakowski said consoles continue to be "necessary to broaden the audience" for casual and semi-casual players. "It’s important to have easy to plug in and enjoy gaming," he said.

He said consoles will "weather the storm" they are currently facing today, including pricing. Nowakowski also said he's heard the rumors that the PS6 and next Xbox could be delayed, but he said, "I don't know if they're true."

Generally speaking, Nowakowski said CD Projekt doesn't spend too much time worrying about how the company reaches people. "Content is the king. And if the content is right, people will find a way to play it," the executive said.

The developers at CD Projekt would ask for "as much power" as possible to help display games in the best possible light. However, Nowakowski said the developers at CD Projekt are "realistic," too, so if next-gen consoles get delayed, some ideas that would require new, more powerful hardware might get "put on a shelf for the future."
"We’d have to adjust. We’re not worried on the commercial side. Consoles are here to stay," he said.
CD Projekt has multiple games in the works that are likely planned for new consoles, as The Witcher 4 is lined up for release in 2028, with Cyberpunk 2 likely coming sometime after.

Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have raised hardware prices due to global market factors, including tariffs and the AI-fueled demand for components and memory. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma recently said it's "wonderful" that GPUs have use cases outside of gaming , even if it means that Xbox consoles are now more expensive than ever. Nintendo, for its part, has received refunds for President Trump's tariffs--which were deemed illegal--but said it has no legal requirement to pass along any money to consumers who paid more. Sony, meanwhile, has received gigantic tariff refunds as well, with no plans to pass anything along .

You still have as much freedom as you had before; you can just do more now, and you have more choice in terms of how you approach situations."

At the highest level, players can have a criminal record that labels them as a "Professional," and from there, the states descend into Aggressive, Violent, and Psycho. Reaching the fifth, currently unnamed state, is said to be particularly tough, but once you do, there's no return from a full descent into villainy. The idea is that players will have the freedom to alternate between criminal profiles or replay the game while aiming to align with those particular states.

title: LOTR Fans Need To “Be Patient,” Kingdom Come Dev Says About New Middle-earth RPG
event_sentences: Kingdom Come developer Warhorse is working on multiple new games, including a The Lord of the Rings role-playing game . We don't know much about it right now, and Warhorse isn't likely to share more details anytime soon.

In a post on social media , Warhorse said, "We're excited to tell you guys more, you've just gotta be patient for now." In short, you should be more like an Ent and slow down. Good things come to those who wait, after all.
Warhorse announced the game earlier this year, saying it will be a "deeply immersive" open-world Middle-earth RPG.

The game will feature a “living world” populated by “interesting characters, memorable places, and, of course, a strong narrative focus," the developers said. This doesn't tell us much about it, but it’s a starting point for understanding where the game may be headed. We also know that Deliverance 2 design director Viktor Bocan is leading the development of the untitled Lord of the Rings game.

As for the Lord of the Rings game series, Tomb Raider studio Crystal Dynamics is said to be working on its own game as well . Both Crystal Dynamics and Warhorse are owned by Embracer, which controls the rights to The Lord of the Rings.
Beyond these games, Aspyr Media has teased more re-releases of classic The Lord of the Rings games following the shadow-drop of War in the North .

The Lord of the Rings series remains popular outside of games, too. Prime Video’s The Rings of Power series returns for a third season this November and Andy Serkis is directing The Hunt for Gollum, which will be out in 2027.

title: Don’t Care About GTA 6’s Romance System? Don’t Use It, Dev Says
event_sentences: GTA 6 's Jason and Lucia can be romantically involved , or they can just be partners in crime. If you're not interested in the game's romance system, don't use it, Rockstar's Rob Nelson said in a new interview.

Players who do wish to grow and nurture a romantic relationship between Jason and Lucia can hold hands, visit a zoo together, or enjoy a romantic stroll on the beach, Nelson said. If players don’t want to do those things, they don’t have to, but Nelson said players might miss out on other things.

"I don’t want to say too much more about this because I don’t want to spoil anything. It really adds a compelling element to things, and it’s one of the reasons we wanted to approach this sort of story, because it's completely different for us," Nelson said. "Could we bring some sort of emotional resonance to GTA for people if they wanted to engage with it? Could we also provide mechanisms for people to just opt out of it if they're not into it? If they feel like, ‘I don't want a relationship in this?’ That's what we're going to find out. It's not something that we want to foist upon players."
Nelson said players might grow to "feel protective of [Jason and Lucia] as a unit" as they progress through the game, and the developers at Rockstar didn't originally envision this.

"This is something we did not know when we started, and it really had to be something we felt our way through. But I will say that whether you’re getting in trouble, or you’re running from the cops, or getting in a car, or waiting for the other one--playing as them together feels very cool. It feels like you’re taking care of them, if that’s something you’re into," he said.
“It’s new for GTA, this idea of your actions having meaning in terms of how you treat your partner or  how violent you are ,” Nelson said in another interview.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. We learned a lot more about the game today, including how  the map is 3X bigger than Red Dead Redemption 2’s  and that  a playthrough can be 80 hours long . The game also brings back  six-star wanted levels , and that  you can pet the dog .

title: You Can Watch A Cow Play Eve Online Right Now
event_sentences: Earlier this summer, Fenris Creations (formerly CCP Games) released an update to its popular online spacefaring MMO called Cradle of War, which the community immediately abbreviated to "CoW." This shorthand apparently sparked a few ideas inside Fenris, and now an actual cow is livestreaming an Eve Online session from Iceland.

The cow, whose name is Valva and username is FC CapitalCowPilot, is manning a mining ship on a deep space mining operation. The team at Fenris Creations fitted its pen with "cow-proof" buttons, which when stepped on will perform certain in-game actions, while a voiceover host delivers cow facts to viewers of the livestream.

As of this writing, over 200 players have joined CapitalCowPilot's mining expedition, with over 4000 viewers watching along on Twitch as the cow moves around its pen. Fenris Creations has announced some community goals which can be unlocked during the stream, including new skins for ships and new updates for the Cradle of War expansion.

The Cradle of War expansion's non-bovine additions include time-limited Military Campaigns, which let players complete tasks in order to advance their empire's goals, and a new area called Exordium specifically built to help onboard new players.

title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe Just Got A Surprise Free Update With 8-Player Split-Screen
event_sentences: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe has been Nintendo's golden goose for several years, as it's the company's best-selling Switch game of all time and has received various updates over the years, becoming a feature-packed experience. Even with Mario Kart World aiming to usurp its position, Nintendo isn't done dropping new content into Mario Kart 8 yet, as the game just received a new eight-player split-screen mode out of nowhere on Switch 2. It's free to download, allows for up to eight players to share the screen locally, and it looks wild in action.

But the expanded local split-screen is the real star of the show here, as not only can you strain your eyes while playing on TV, but you can also make your local optometrist happy by watching all those races unfold in handheld mode on the Switch 2. Considering just how much of an intensive load it is to render eight sessions in real time, the new multiplayer mode is a technical marvel to watch.

This will likely keep Mario Kart 8 Deluxe at the top of the Nintendo food chain for a while yet. Mario Kart World has its charm, but as fans have pointed out, the anemic amount of content added since its launch last year has made it hard to root for. That drought might be coming to a temporary end, as with a rumored Nintendo Direct  supposedly arriving later this month, players are expecting Mario Kart World to get some sort of an update. If you're looking to grab it, a new Switch 2 + Mario Kart World bundle ($550) launches in late September--albeit for $50 when compared to the original launch bundle.

title: Former id Software producer says the team faced the 'worst crunch' in the series' history on Doom: The Dark Ages – Revelations: 'There were days where I didn't see my son'
event_sentences: The situation surrounding Doom: The Dark Ages – Revelations was already grim. Id Software put out a fantastic expansion that addressed many issues present in the ( still pretty good ) base game, placing it among the best works the FPS specialists have ever produced. The reward for many of The Dark Ages team was to be instantly laid off , as Xbox cut 136 members of the studio's workforce.

Now, it also appears that getting Revelations to the finish line was a punishing experience for those involved, at least according to former id Software producer Andrew Willis. Speaking on the Kiwi Talkz podcast for Insider Gaming , Willis revealed that the team experienced a gnarly level of crunch in the months leading up to Revelations' release.

"It was tight," Willis explained. "There were two months where I was working something like at least 12 hours every day. I know I hit 17 a couple of days." Willis goes on to describe the experience as "brutal" and says that most of the expansion was put together "in three or four months."

That's a ridiculously short turnaround for an expansion that's around six hours long, especially when you consider the main game—which runs at about 20 hours—took five years to build. Revelations' development timeframe was meant to be even shorter. But Willis says the expansion encountered feature-creep, with new elements being added as the DLC was built.

"There were days where I didn't get to see my son the whole day; multiple days of that that I sacrificed to get this out the door at the level of quality," Willis continues. He says that everybody on the team had a similar experience, and that even veteran designers from both the game and film industries were shocked by the level of crunch involved. "We had people that worked in Hollywood for 20 years and game development for 10 and said that this was the worst crunch they'd been a part of."

Willis was one of the many id Software devs laid off as part of Microsoft's massive cuts , in which it slashed 1,600 jobs (with another 1,600 being cut over the next fiscal year) and numerous studios like Compulsion Games and Double Fine were cut loose from Xbox Game Studios. Apparently, the Revelations team learned about the layoffs the day before the expansion was due to launch.
"You spend so much of your energy and hours of your life, and sacrifice a bunch of things to get something out of the door, and then they lay you off," Willis said. "It's such a wild feeling."

(Image credit: Xbox) It all sounds pretty unpleasant, and it makes one wonder what the situation at id Software was like after The Dark Ages' release to make it so desperate to rush an expansion out of the door. Was this an internal decision? Or a consequence of pressure from the higher-ups at Xbox? Statistics suggest that The Dark Ages sold significantly fewer copies than 2020's Doom Eternal , though this was to be expected given that The Dark Ages released day one on Game Pass.
As for what's happening with id Software more broadly, Hugo Martin insisted that the studio is fine in the wake of Microsoft's layoffs.

title: 30,000 games are either Steam Deck verified or at least 'playable' on Valve's handheld
event_sentences: Valve's handheld launched in February 2022, opening the door to playing your Steam library on the go. Now, almost half a decade later, 30,000 games either enjoy the green stamp of being Steam Deck verified, or are at least considered 'playable.'

'Verified' means your game of choice should work great on the Steam Deck from first boot, whereas 'Playable' games require either some finagling or adjustments for the best experience. Steam Deck verification is also joined by similar compatibility checks for the Steam Machine , the soon-to-be-released Steam Frame , and SteamOS more broadly. I make the whole thing sound straightforward, but it's worth noting that the Steam Deck's full verification criteria can present developers with confusing hoops to jump through .

And it doesn't mean games will always be playable on the Steam Deck. Ubisoft recently announced that it is "removing For Honor from the Linux platform to ensure a safer environment for our players as we cannot meaningfully deploy protection on this platform." Which means no third-person melee fun for you on Steam Deck, so from September 10 there will be one less game playable on Steam Deck.

Anyway, for a bit more context, SteamDB also says well over 130,000 games total have been released on Steam to date. SteamDB's figures suggest there were half as many games on Steam back in 2022. With the platform having grown so significantly in just the last four years, the days of 10% of all Steam games enjoying official Steam Deck compatibility feel so long ago.

Click to build a house and it'll quickly be constructed in a colorful shower of Lego bricks falling from the sky and piling up into a cozy-looking little home. The cute animations and cheery visuals are exactly what I'd hoped for when I saw the game's trailer last week, and again made me wonder why Lego didn't make a city builder years ago.

As in builders like Cities: Skylines (Paradox Interactive is publishing this one, too), you drag roads out across the ground and connect buildings to them: houses, shops, farms, and factories. One thing I noticed, in this build at least, is that the map is almost entirely a flat plane, with only a few areas I could see where the elevation changed a bit. I didn't see any terrain manipulation tools in the build, either, which is a little disappointing.

A lot of the focus is on customizing each of the buildings you place. You can boost a homeowner's happiness by decorating their yard with items like mailboxes, barbeques, flowers, wheelbarrows, fountains, and all sorts of little prebuilt odds and ends. But each household also has a specific taste, called Flavor.

(Image credit: Paradox Interactive) Choosing decorations from the Flavor categories listed, like "cozy" or "nature," will increase the household's happiness. Flavor is optional—it's a city builder, after all, and not everyone wants to obsess over the micro-details—but if you want to make every single citizen in your city overjoyed with their home, you've got the tools to do it.

I also got to tinker with, very lightly, the resource chains in Lego Skylines. I built a couple of farms that generate raw goods, which are then shipped to factories to make products, which are then sold in shops. There wasn't much to it, logistically: just having the farm, factory, and stores placed seemed like enough to get the supply chain up and running, and soon little trucks were making deliveries and pickups without my input. But I was pretty pleased that my bread factory resembled a giant toaster, complete with two enormous slices of toast sticking out of the roof. Pretty much everything in Lego Skylines is completely cute.

I hope I get the chance to play more soon. It's a lovely game to look at and if you like focusing on little details in your builders, like decorating individual houses and fussing over the themes of neighborhoods, it looks like there'll be a lot here to keep you occupied. For people more into a deep city building challenge, I'm guessing this isn't the city builder for you, but we'll find out when we get to play some more.

title: Was Geralt's voice actor inspired by Henry Cavill's take on him in The Witcher series? 'No, because we were first'

title: I've been worried Persona is succumbing to saminess, but Persona 4 Revival feels just as good as its predecessor did 16 years ago
event_sentences: Persona 3 Reload was the first utilisation of that template, and now we're doing it all over again with Persona 4 Revival. Its cast of characters un-chibified, ready to be unleashed upon a far more highly detailed rendition of the cosy town of Inaba.

I'm incredibly relieved to say that the answer to that is: it absolutely does. It's a little different, sure—most of the English voice cast has been swapped out, the soundtrack has been re-recorded and rearranged, and I'm still not totally sold on its updated character portraits (seriously, where is Yosuke's jawline?)

But as I played my way through small snippets of the game's early hours—retreading the familiar territory of Yukiko's castle and facing off against Shadow Chie—I was getting those same giddy feelings that I felt the first time I booted up Persona 4 Golden on my PS Vita.

(Image credit: Atlus) That doesn't mean there aren't new things to awe at and explore for veterans of Inaba's streets, mind you. The foggy town is now fully explorable in 3D, and plodding up and down its winding roads revealed to me a faithfully recreated space with all the fun details and finesse that older hardware couldn't afford. It's still got those wonderful vibes that teeter between cosy and mildly unsettling.

The game's modern makeover truly shines in the heart of Persona 4 Revival's battles. The shadow designs are fantastic— the tongue-lolling Hablerie looks even more disturbing in the best possible way, and the extra details and textures on Shadow Chie make its already-incredible visuals pop. Pretty much every shadow has been elevated with a few tweaks here and there instead of going for full-blown remakes, a decision I'm really pleased about.

(Image credit: Atlus) Then there's the actual combat stuff. The classic "1 More" system returns, but it's now folded in with Persona 5's Baton Pass that lets you pass the extra attack onto an ally. There's also a brand-new mechanic that lets you send shadows flying into each other to pass on status ailments and deal extra damage, something I didn't get to play around with in my time with the demo but I'm very excited about regardless.

Prime Time seems to be the main addition to combat, another one I didn't really get to use during the demo—filling a gauge lets you perform a whole bunch of actions and skills without coughing up the HP or MP for them, as well as ignoring resistances and freely using Baton Passes. It seems like something that's going to be utterly broken as a concept, and I'm interested in seeing how Atlus plans on balancing something that seems so bonkers powerful.

Mostly, I'm just ridiculously excited to jump back in and play more. Persona 5 may be the most well-known in the series at this point, but Persona 4 is easily my favourite in terms of raw vibes and storytelling. Being able to recapture that feeling 16 years after Golden is no easy feat, but from the small parts of Revival I've played so far, Atlus has absolutely nailed it.

title: SteamDB changes hands to Nexus Mods, which means it 'needs to make money' now—but there won't be ads or paywalls
event_sentences: SteamDB is an excellent resource—as someone who occasionally has to pull up a game's concurrent numbers or pricing to make a point, I'd be lying if I said I haven't used it in a professional capacity. What's been more staggering is its status as a site run entirely on donations.

Well, that's ending soon. The site's founder, xPaw, has decided to move on due to a feeling of burnout. In their full statement , they write: "After Covid and with the rise of AI, the internet we once loved is gone, and with it my passion. I have started experiencing burnout with the project, but I powered through.

The buyers in question? NexusMods, which has its own sister announcement on its site that details its motivations, which are twofold. Firstly, having the information SteamDB has collated over the years is useful: "We have already started collecting Steam game data ourselves, but once an update is pushed, manifests and data for the old versions become much more difficult to access. SteamDB already does this far better than we can, and has a massive back-catalogue to draw from."

In a FAQ , NexusMods cops to this being a consideration going forward: "We're going to be straight about this rather than dance around it: yes, SteamDB needs to make money. What xPaw has built—and kept running largely through personal dedication and community donations—is an extraordinary achievement.
"Giving it the team, infrastructure and long-term investment it deserves is how we protect that work and ensure SteamDB can thrive for the next decade and beyond."

title: The Expanse: Osiris Reborn turns the best Mass Effect mission into an entire game
event_sentences: We already wrote about The Expanse's hi-tech fights after checking it out in April. "I was worried Owlcat couldn't pull off Mass Effect-style cinematic action in its big new RPG, but after an hour of blowing stuff up in The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, I'm feeling very reassured," Robin said back then. And I'm feeling the same way.

Mass Effect took three games to get its shooting up to snuff, but The Expanse might have nailed it on the first go. It's more responsive, varied, and you can order your teammates to pull off some explosively neat tricks. They're called exploits, and depending on who you have in your three-person squad, you'll see different parts of the environment highlighted in red—these are places where your pals can do their thing.

(Image credit: Owlcat Games) J, my identical twin who serves as the first companion, seems to mostly enjoy blowing things up. Usually that means cover. I was fighting Protogen goons—the villainous Earth corporation—and took every opportunity to stop them from cowardly hiding behind walls. But I also used J to take out bridges, a lift and other objects, with each instance rewarding me with a spectacular explosion and some dead foes.

When I needed to get into a crate, for instance, I failed to persuade a Protogen employee that it didn't matter that I had no paperwork. My persuasion skill wasn't high enough. But I was able to download some documents from a terminal, which one of my pals onboard my ship used to create a forgery.

If you've watched the show or read the books, you'll be rewarded for your foreknowledge with plenty of little nods here and there—especially when you're snooping around and reading everyone's emails. But if this is all new to you, it'll just appear to be worldbuilding rather than gatekeeping.

(Image credit: Owlcat Games) The demo ended on a cliffhanger, with my squad ready to pull off an audacious plan to stop a protomolecule mutant from doing more damage. I was ready to get stuck in, and then the "Thanks for playing" message appeared. It was devastating. I had to rush to another appointment anyway, but if Owlcat said "Nah, it's cool, you can play more," I don't think I would have been able to decline.
I guess I'll just have to wait until next year! The Expanse: Osiris Reborn should be appearing in the second quarter of 2027.

title: 半个多月预约猛增至7000万，腾讯“王牌”不藏了：定档9月10日
event_sentences: 就在刚刚落幕的“王牌定档秀”上，《 王者万象棋 》正式官宣预约量突破7000万大关，并同时定档于9月10日正式上线。
这份预约数据的含金量，远不止“超过策略对战品类赛道常规水准”这么简单——即便放眼整个策略品类，都很难说有这么多玩家。
更惊人的是增速：放在近一年国内已知上线新游的行列当中，月初曝光的5000万预约量已经是足够罕见的数据高位，而不到短短一个月，这个数字便猛增2000万，直接刷新了一个新的峰值，足以印证玩家们对这款产品的热忱期待。
说来其实我一直有点儿好奇：这次定档，万象棋并没有沿用传统发布会的叫法，反倒用了一个很有氛围感的词——“秀”。
明明一份定档公告就能解决的事儿，何必要搞出这么大的阵仗？
直到我仔细一看，发现台上吕布的 Coser 不是别人，正是吕布绝活主播“吕德华”，再回想起此前测试阶段的实际体验，我才读懂万象棋决心要作的“秀”究竟指向了什么—— 它想让每一个王者玩家，都能够用自己的本命英雄“秀”出高光。
这场定档“秀”的内涵也远不止于此，另一个引人注目的地方在于：万象棋上线时即直接首发85位王者英雄——这一数字直接打破了同类产品棋子“慢上线，拉周期”的常规节奏，不仅意味着绝大多数老玩家坐上棋局的第一时间，就能与自己心心念念的本命英雄重逢，直接从熟悉英雄的全新可能性切入，在老熟人的陪伴下开启棋局，无需经历漫长的等待，也同时拉满了阵容搭配的多样性，留足了广阔的套路开发空间。
以高人气英雄角色李白为原型的万象棋白歌，便保留了各种辨识度极高的角色视觉特征，老玩家一眼便能够认出角色原型；同时，万象棋还赋予其热爱文学、喜好旅游的自由撰稿人设定，鲜活又充满现代气息，上线测试阶段便有大量玩家直呼“又萌又帅”。
除了为王者IP补齐更加丰富立体的玩法场景，再结合定档秀释放的一系列重磅信息，不难看出，万象棋还怀揣着更大的野心——它想要做的，是一个全新的王者IP生态策源地，打造越发扎实的IP文化生态。
最夺人眼球的，便是定档秀上公布的大量福利内容。
除了和小王的联动，万象棋同样准备了大量上线福利：累计50抽夺宝，嬴律“优雅恋人”和乔汐“行鲤绯梦”的棋手皮肤，“演武沙盘”和“万象超市”的两个棋盘，以及头像框、动态表情......基本都是上线或参与游戏活动就送。
接连登场的各类联动企划，也一波接一波引爆了定档秀的讨论热度：既有水豚噜噜这类IP联动，也有茶话弄、滴滴青桔、加多宝等跨界合作，更有与华润万象生活的重磅线下合作。
可以预见的是，随着万象棋正式上线，这片由千万玩家们共同撑起的“万象之都”，将为王者IP注入源源不断的生命力，而每一位玩家，也都将见证并参与这部IP故事篇章的崭新未来。

title: 刚刚，我们玩到了米哈游口中“不像米哈游”的新产品
event_sentences: 《源初之结》 试玩刚结束，我又把那部首曝PV点开重看了一遍。
就在前一天的2026科隆游戏展开幕之夜，作为全场第一个亮相的产品，米哈游的《源初之结》上来便直接炸场，褪去惯用的卡通渲染，以截然不同的美术质量与精致又写实的画面风格，狠狠在科隆上当了一回显眼包，PV相关内容的具体解析可参见 游戏日报 前日发布的报道文章。
通过此前发布的游戏PV，相信大伙应该已经有所了解，《源初之结》的世界观设定是比较宏大的，以多元神话作为核心创作题材，将不同地区玩家耳熟能详的经典神话意象熔于一炉。
接下来，便是“合作共斗”概念的呈现。
育碧魁北克公司关卡设计师Thierry Lauret曾提出过这样一个观点，他认为，多人游戏的合作模式无外乎四种类型：The gate（各自行动，必要时配合）、The comfort（非强制，仅为舒适度服务）、The class（角色能力不完整，机制互补）、The job（玩家任务不同，但空间相同），分别对应着不同的玩法侧重方向。
如果参照这个逻辑，就游戏日报看来，《源初之结》的共斗合作侧重方向大概介于“comfort”与“class”之间，即单人也能玩，非强制组队；但当组成了一个职业分工明确的团队时，整体的游戏体验与乐趣将存在质的提升。
他们表示，游戏大部分核心内容均支持单人畅玩，前中期玩法均可单人体验，也将同时开放多人合作模式，其核心乐趣在于团队配合与社交互动，能提供单人模式之外的差异化体验。
这是在游戏设计理念上“合作共斗”概念的表现。
从《崩坏3》成为国产3D二次元动作手游先河，到《原神》开创二游开放世界的全新赛道，米哈游的势头从未被已然取得的商业成绩所牵绊，反而更加快了其覆盖各品类差异化产品赛道的脚步，而《源初之结》，也只是米哈游“突破自我”这条应行之路上一个全新的节点罢了。
